title: Call: CDPH Food and Drug Branch — Three Illnesses, Ship-To List Requested

fields.systemName: Recorded Line - Food Safety & Quality, Plant 1

caller.name: Marisol Ortega, Investigator
caller.label: California Department of Public Health, Food and Drug Branch

callee.name: Dr. Imani Brooks
callee.label: VP Food Safety and Quality / Recall Coordinator

transcript.speaker: CDPH Investigator
transcript.text: Good morning. This is Marisol Ortega, investigator with the Food and Drug Branch at the California Department of Public Health. Am I speaking with Dr. Brooks?

transcript.speaker: CDPH Investigator
transcript.text: Thank you. I'll get right to it. We have three reported cases of E. coli O157:H7 illness. Two are in Sacramento County, and one is in Reno, which came to us through our Nevada counterparts. Two of the three report eating bagged chopped romaine in the days before they got sick. Whole-genome sequencing is pending, so nothing is linked yet. We understand you have a presumptive positive on a retained sample. Can you confirm which lots you're holding?

transcript.speaker: CDPH Investigator
transcript.text: Okay. I've written down five lots. We're requesting your distribution list for those lots at the ship-to level. That means every location that received product, with quantities and ship dates. Send it as soon as you can. Honestly, whatever you have now is better than a perfect list tomorrow. Can you email it this morning? What time should I expect it?

transcript.speaker: CDPH Investigator
transcript.text: That works. Send it to fdb.investigations@cdph-fdb.example with my name in the subject line, and copy me at marisol.ortega@cdph-fdb.example. If something on the list changes after you send it, send an updated version. Don't wait. Who should I call if I have questions about the data, you or someone on your traceability side?

transcript.speaker: CDPH Investigator
transcript.text: Got it. My direct line is (916) 555-0142. I'll be at my desk all morning. We'll be in touch once sequencing comes back, and please call me the moment your confirmation result is in, either way. Thanks, Dr. Brooks.

voiceStyles.CDPH Investigator: Woman in her 50s, calm, measured and businesslike; quiet state office, keyboard typing now and then while she takes notes

instructorNote: This call turns the presumptive into a public health event: reported illnesses shorten the regulatory timeline and strengthen the Class I case for Phase 3. Watch for RECALL to log the call (who, what, when) under Log Everything, read back the five lot codes and commit to a send time. Also watch for TRACE to build the PLCTR 5 sheet, with the 60 unreconciled cases and the Rivermark paper lots on a gaps tab rather than left out, and for RECALL to review the sheet before it goes to CDPH.
